dedupe_keys.name: network model of the us petrochemical industry under raw material and hurricane harvey disruptions 2019

description: This model represents the US chemical industry in 2017 as a geographically resolved network of production units and computes optimal chemical flows between them by linear programming. Besides a baseline, it runs three disruption scenarios: primary raw material disruptions, the ethylene cracker outages reported during Hurricane Harvey, and assumed capacity losses along Harvey's storm track, showing how the industry's structure adapts to widespread or local disruptions. In the assumed Harvey case, 170 chemical units in 26 states changed production because of supply chain effects. It was developed by Sean E. DeRosa, Yosuke Kimura, Mark A. Stadtherr, Gary McGaughey, Elena McDonald-Buller and David T. Allen of Sandia National Laboratories and the University of Texas at Austin and published in Industrial and Engineering Chemistry Research in July 2019. Coverage is national. The accepted manuscript is available free online through the Department of Energy's public access repository; no licence is stated and the model data are not released. Caveats: it assumes optimal rerouting of flows, which real plants cannot always achieve, and uses 2017 capacities. For simulation it shows how hurricane outages on the Gulf Coast cascade through petrochemical supply chains across the country. It is related to the CSB Arkema Crosby Hurricane Harvey flooding case study record in this catalogue.
